docRequirement: hooks.md § "SessionStart decision control" (lines 981-992) binds a SessionStart hook's exit-0 JSON to FIVE event-specific output fields, not one: `additionalContext`, plus `initialUserMessage` ("String used as the first user message of the session"), `sessionTitle` ("Sets the session title, with the same effect as `/rename`… Applies when `source` is `"startup"`, `"resume"`, or `"fork"`; ignored on `"clear"` and `"compact"`"), `watchPaths` ("Array of absolute paths to watch for FileChanged events during this session") and `reloadSkills` ("Boolean. When `true`, Claude Code re-scans the skill and command directories after the SessionStart hooks complete, so skills the hook installed are available in the same session, starting with the first prompt"). Line 874's event table corroborates: "SessionStart also accepts [`initialUserMessage`, `watchPaths`, `sessionTitle`, and `reloadSkills`]… No blocking or decision control". The documented example nests all of them under `hookSpecificOutput` alongside `hookEventName: "SessionStart"`.

divergence:
Not a key-name mismatch and not a wrong value — four of the five documented SessionStart output keys are absent from the codebase entirely, at the parser, at the per-event surface table, and at the decision type. `additionalContext` is correct end-to-end. Consequence: a SessionStart hook returning any of the four exits 0, its JSON parses, and every one of those fields is discarded with no warning anywhere.

The four are not one gap but three shapes:
- `sessionTitle` and `reloadSkills` are pure wiring — parser + surface + a host callback; both target mechanisms already exist (`renameSession`, `invalidateSkillsCache`/`capabilityResolver.invalidate`).
- `initialUserMessage` needs an ordering change, not just a parse: `apps/cli/src/index.ts:764-770` `cmdRun` exits 1 with "No prompt provided" BEFORE any server or session is created, so no SessionStart hook has run at the point the doc says the hook may supply the turn (hooks.md:1077).
- `watchPaths` needs a subsystem that does not exist. Nessy's `FileChanged` is driven by file-mutating tool completion, not a disk watcher (`packages/shared/src/automations/types.ts:73`: ordering "after a file mutation completes"), a limit already reasoned about at `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-inert-unit-b.md:329-331`: "there is no watch list to build and no `watchPaths` output to honour".

blastRadius:
Crosses a package boundary AND a persistence/wire boundary — a risk trigger by this repo's rules.

Parse/contract layer: `parseHookCommandOutput` has 7 callers (`automations/automation-system.ts`, `automations/hook-command.ts`, `plugins/hooks-automation.ts`); `parseHookOutputForEvent` has 8 (`automation-system.ts`, `hooks-automation.ts`, `automations/index.ts`); `projectHookDecisionForEvent`/`hookDecisionPattern` are read by every emission-site gate. Widening `PreToolUseDecision` widens `HookDecisionField` for all fifteen-odd events, but no other event's `fields` list changes, so no other surface widens — verify by leaving the FileChanged half of `hook-decision-contract.test.ts:101-107` green. Covering tests: `automations/hook-command.test.ts`, `automations/hook-decision-contract.test.ts`, `automations/task-hooks.test.ts`.

Wire/persistence: `renameSession` (`SessionManager.ts:14112-14126`) writes the session record (`persistSession`), emits `{ type: 'title_generated' }` to the renderer, and pokes the config watcher's session-partition seam. A hook can now rename a session — that is user-visible state a hook did not previously touch. `capabilityResolver.invalidate(… 'revoke-active-snapshot')` revokes the ACTIVE capability snapshot mid-session; the pi path also carries capability-generation leases (`pi-agent.ts:1869`, `:2309-2317`, `base-agent.ts:2509`), so a reload fired at the wrong point in a turn could invalidate a lease under an in-flight tool. Firing it only at the pre-manifest-sync point (`pi-agent.ts:6540`, before `:6573`) is what keeps that safe.

SDK surface: `SdkAutomationCallbackResult` (`types.ts:907`) is the shape handed to the Claude Agent SDK's hook callbacks via `claude-agent.ts:1288`; new fields there are visible to the SDK, not just to us.

Imported-plugin path: Claude plugin hooks bound to SessionStart arrive through `plugins/hooks-automation.ts` (`SessionStart: 'SessionStart'` at :375) and share the same parser, so an imported plugin hook gains the behaviour with no adapter change.

DO NOT TOUCH `packages/shared/src/plugins/hooks-runtime.ts:241` `parseHookOutput`. It is an identically-shaped second executor that is unreachable in production, and reviving it is a recorded owner decision against: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` §3 item 5, "Do not revive `hooks-runtime.ts`… Fixing the dead path and believing the bug closed is the specific trap here."
userImpact:
Observable today, silently. A user writes a SessionStart automation (or installs a Claude plugin whose SessionStart hook does this) that prints the documented object — `{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"SessionStart","sessionTitle":"auth-refactor","reloadSkills":true}}` — the hook exits 0, the transcript shows no error and no warning, and nothing happens: the session keeps its auto-generated name in the sidebar, and any skill the hook just installed or `git pull`ed into the skills directory is absent from the model's tools for the whole session, appearing only after a restart. hooks.md's own `reloadSkills` worked example is exactly a team-skills `git pull`, so the doc's headline recipe for shared skills is inert here — that is the sharpest of the four.

`initialUserMessage`: `nessy-general-agent run` with no prompt exits 1 with "No prompt provided" even when a SessionStart hook would have supplied the first turn.

`watchPaths`: none observable, and it would stay none even if parsed — there is no disk watcher for it to configure. It surfaces only after a real path watcher exists behind FileChanged.
